item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that its Supreme Standing Committee for Human Rights monitored implementation of international obligations, proposed legislative and procedural measures, and supervised implementation; it also reported a National Human Rights Strategy for 2021–2026 covering civil and political rights, socioeconomic rights, vulnerable groups, and human-rights education.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.10","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The institutional arrangements predated 2023 but were reported as operating through the end of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these measures to the Egyptian Government; direct personal involvement by Abdel Fattah el-Sisi is not specified, although the measures occurred under his presidency.","limitations":["This is a government report and does not independently verify implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that it adopted a comprehensive migration approach, placed migrants' human rights at the core of its efforts, and used Egypt Vision 2030 to envisage services for migrants and refugees.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.3","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The policy was described as continuing through 2023; Egypt Vision 2030 was updated in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Government policy under the presidency of Abdel Fattah el-Sisi; the document does not identify a personal presidential directive for each measure.","limitations":["The report states policy aims and institutional claims rather than independently measured welfare outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the Ministry of Labour monitored and inspected enterprises, concluded bilateral labour agreements, expanded vocational-training centres, and modernized 130 of 300 recruitment bureaux; 251 recruitment firms were newly licensed, 1,231 licences renewed, and 112 revoked, leaving 1,482 licensed firms.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report covers developments through the end of 2023, but several measures began earlier and some were still underway.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Egyptian Government and Ministry of Labour under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The report does not provide independent inspection results, compliance rates, or distributional effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported bilateral labour agreements with Jordan and Greece, vocational-examination agreements with Saudi Arabia, and labour and employment agreements with Italy, alongside online employment links for Jordan and Libya.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The Jordan operational programme covered 2023–2024; the report otherwise describes agreements existing by the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The agreements are attributed to the Egyptian Government; no personal presidential role is identified.","limitations":["The source does not quantify jobs created, enforcement, or worker outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that 112 recruitment-firm licences were revoked while firms were monitored and supervised, indicating some enforcement against non-compliant labour intermediaries.","question_ids":["5B.5","6B.7","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The figure is presented in the report covering implementation through 2023, without a precise revocation date.","ruler_attribution":"The enforcement is attributed to the Ministry of Labour under the Egyptian Government.","limitations":["The source does not state the grounds for revocation or whether affected workers received remedies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the Ministry of Labour expanded and renovated vocational-training centres and invested in skills development, mutual recognition of qualifications, and employment opportunities for young people and migrants.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The measures were reported as part of the period ending in 2023, though the source gives no completion date for all activities.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Government and Ministry of Labour under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["No budget, coverage, completion, or employment-outcome data are provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that it had concluded agreements for seasonal agricultural employment in Greece, including a 2022 agreement envisaging 5,000 first-year job opportunities, and agreements with Germany concerning vocational education, migration, reintegration, and regular migration channels.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The Greece agreement was in its first trial year during the reporting period; the report was submitted in 2024 and covers through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The agreements are attributed to the Egyptian Government; the source does not establish personal presidential authorship.","limitations":["The source does not show how many opportunities were actually filled or their effects on income and migration."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that 130 of 300 recruitment bureaux had been modernized and connected online to the Ministry of Labour, while recruitment firms were licensed, renewed, or revoked under government supervision.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report presents this as an operational status during the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measure is attributed to the Ministry of Labour under the Egyptian Government.","limitations":["The source does not independently assess accessibility, processing times, or corruption risks."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that it had adopted or launched national strategies for women, anti-corruption, human rights, trafficking prevention, and updated Egypt Vision 2030 in November 2023.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","6B.3","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The strategies span earlier years, while the updated Egypt Vision 2030 was launched in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The strategies are attributed to Egyptian state institutions during el-Sisi's presidency; the source does not establish his personal authorship for each strategy.","limitations":["The source lists strategies and launch dates but gives limited evidence of completed outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported an integrated anti-trafficking system involving increased penalties, specialized criminal chambers, geographic mapping, guidance for officials and workers, police-academy training, embassy training, awareness campaigns, improved hotline capacity, and development of a secure shelter and referral mechanism for women and child victims.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The measures were reported as operating during the period ending in 2023, with some initiatives still under development.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Egyptian Government and relevant ministries; direct presidential action is not specified.","limitations":["The source does not report trafficking prevalence, conviction rates, shelter use, or victim outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that its national coordinating committee criminalized migrant smuggling and protected irregular migrants and witnesses through a dedicated fund, while the National Council for Childhood and Motherhood represented unaccompanied children whose families could not be identified.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The legal and institutional arrangements were in force during the reporting period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to Egyptian state institutions under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The source does not quantify fund disbursements, cases assisted, or implementation gaps."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":18,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that approximately 420,000 refugees and asylum-seekers registered with UNHCR were hosted in Egypt, that facilities were provided for an estimated 380,000 Sudanese citizens entering after the Sudan crisis, and that foreign residents and migrants received access to primary health care and national campaigns.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The Sudanese-arrival figure and service claims concern the reporting period through 2023; the broader refugee figure is a contemporaneous estimate.","ruler_attribution":"The hosting and service measures are attributed to the Egyptian Government under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The source is Egypt's self-report and does not establish the quality, geographic equity, or actual uptake of services."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":18,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that migrant and refugee children were integrated into Egyptian education, with 87,696 migrant and refugee students enrolled in State-run or private schools and Syrian, Yemeni, and Palestinian students exempt from tuition fees.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The enrollment figure is reported for the period covered, although the cited academic-year data are earlier than 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The education policies are attributed to Egyptian authorities and presidential-office instructions under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The source does not provide attendance, completion, learning, or access data for 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the legal framework included the Anti-Human Trafficking Act, Civil Service Act, Irregular Migration and Migrant Smuggling Act, Persons with Disabilities Act, Social Insurance and Pensions Act, and other measures relevant to migrant-worker protection.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.3","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The laws predated 2023 but were identified as the framework governing the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was enacted by Egyptian state institutions during el-Sisi's presidency; the source does not attribute each law personally to him.","limitations":["Listing laws does not establish enforcement or practical remedy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":20,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported a 2019 criminal-code amendment defining bullying and making it punishable by at least six months' imprisonment and/or a fine of LE 10,000–30,000; it also reported prosecution and conviction of two persons for bullying and assaulting a South Sudanese child, with two years' imprisonment and a LE 100,000 fine.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The prosecution and amendment predated 2023 but were presented as evidence of the legal framework operating during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the amendment and prosecution to Egyptian Government and judicial institutions; it reports that the President publicly honoured the child victim.","limitations":["This is one reported case and does not establish broader enforcement consistency."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that administrative courts overturned Interior Ministry decisions placing foreigners on no-entry lists or ordering deportation, including decisions where statutory time limits had expired or family-unity considerations applied.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","6B.8","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The cited rulings were from 2007–2021 but were reported as part of the legal safeguards applicable through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The rulings concern executive decisions under the Egyptian state; they provide evidence of judicial review but do not establish the President's response to each ruling.","limitations":["The cases are historical examples and do not measure the frequency or effectiveness of judicial remedies in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":32,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that a new civil-society law and regulations provided for establishing associations, encouraged their work, increased exemptions and advantages, and allowed more than 34,000 national and foreign NGOs to apply to regularize their status; 238 bodies remained unregistered.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.7","4B.10","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The law and regularization process were reported as current during the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Egyptian Government and legislature under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The source does not state how applications were adjudicated, whether unregistered groups faced penalties, or whether civic space expanded in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":32,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that NGO foreign funding reached LE 2.5 billion in 2021, compared with LE 2.2 billion in 2020 and LE 1.1 billion in 2019, while domestic grants and donations approached LE 5 billion; NGOs were also consulted in drafting the National Human Rights Strategy.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","6B.9","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The quantitative figures are earlier than 2023, but the source presents them as background to the institutional situation during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The funding and consultation claims are attributed to the Egyptian Government under el-Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The figures do not show the distribution of funding, independence of recipients, or whether consultation changed policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":34,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the national coordinating committee and State Prosecution conducted training on trafficking and migrant smuggling; between October 2019 and June 2023, State Prosecution organized 29 courses for 577 prosecutors, and a June 2023 regional forum addressed digital evidence in transnational trafficking cases.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The training totals include activity through June 2023 and are directly relevant to the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The activities are attributed to State Prosecution and the national coordinating committee under the Egyptian Government.","limitations":["Training participation does not demonstrate improved investigations, convictions, or victim protection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":30,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that its agreement with Greece envisaged 5,000 seasonal agricultural jobs in its first trial year and that agreements with Germany supported vocational education, regular migration channels, reintegration, and modern equipment for border-control agencies.","question_ids":["2B.8","5B.4","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The agreements and first trial year were relevant to the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The agreements are attributed to the Egyptian Government; the source does not specify personal presidential direction.","limitations":["The source does not report actual job placements, procurement details, or border-control effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":32,"end_unit":32,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that a presidential decree in 2021 lifted the nationwide state of emergency through a decree dated 25 October 2021.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.9","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The measure remained relevant during 2023 because the emergency had been lifted before the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The document explicitly attributes the decree to the President of Egypt, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.","limitations":["Ending the nationwide emergency does not establish that other extraordinary security powers or restrictive practices ceased."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":29,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that a 2023 Interior Ministry decree granted 10-year residence cards to foreigners with special residence and five-year cards to those with ordinary residence, including some foreigners unable to obtain passports or travel documents.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The decree was issued in 2023 and directly fits the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The decree was issued by the Interior Minister; the source does not attribute it personally to el-Sisi.","limitations":["The source does not report the number of beneficiaries or whether implementation was uniform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-08a8e399ce77ae66","start_unit":30,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported ongoing cooperation with Germany and Italy on vocational training and skills development for groups considered most prone to migration, alongside a German-Egyptian job, migration, and reintegration centre intended to open regular migration channels.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The cooperation was reported as ongoing during the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The cooperation is attributed to the Egyptian Government; no direct presidential role is specified.","limitations":["The source does not provide completion, budget, or outcome evidence."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is an Egyptian Government periodic report submitted in 2024 and contains substantial historical and self-reported material; facts were retained only where they materially informed a supplied 1B–8B lens for the 2023 period.","The document contains no material evidence on nuclear risk, interstate war decisions, arms control, proliferation, or most ruler-specific integrity questions; no records were created for those topics.","The source rarely distinguishes Abdel Fattah el-Sisi personally from the Egyptian Government, ministries, courts, or legislature; ruler attribution is therefore qualified where personal direction is not explicit."]}
